newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTP volatility expected to head higher.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTP volatility expected to head higher.

text.p: Implied volatility of over-the-counter (OTC) options on Italian cash bonds held steady on Thursday but some brokers expect it to start heading higher.

Uncertainty over whether Italy can really make it into the first round of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999 will begin to take its toll, ending a sizzling seven month rally in the underlying cash market, they say.
"I think volatility will rebound," said an OTC options broker at a U.S. bank in Milan. "The market is quite nervous, all these rumours against convergence trades, the lira re-entering the ERM."
Investors have made handsome profits this year betting that Italian bond yields will converge on German Bunds as Italy whips itself into economic shape to meet the EMU criteria.
But some analysts say these trades may begin to unravel next year as investors take a closer look at Italy's books.

Indeed recent forecasts from the European Commission put Italy's budget deficit at 3.3 percent of GDP in 1997 while EMU criteria calls for 3.0 percent. Its total indebtedness to GDP will be 122.3 percent versus a needed 60 percent.
Data out earlier this session showed Italian wage inflation at 3.7 percent in October, up from 3.6 percent in September.

The broker quoted implied volatility of one-month options on 10-year cash bonds at around 9.5 percent on a price basis, steady on they week. On a yield basis, volatility was around 19.1 percent for one month options.
Benchmark 10-year bonds were quoted at 108.18 at 1104 GMT, down from 108.22 at the end of European trade on Wednesday.
"Everyone is looking to buy volatility not to sell," the broker in Milan said. "I think the market can reach 10.0 to 10.5 percent."
He said he would advise customers to go long volatility of options on 10-year Italian bonds and short volatility of options on five year bonds.
Brokers said implied volatility of options on LIFFE fell this week amid quiet dealings but was also likely to head higher after the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.

"Volatility has been offered right down to 8.4 percent, probably because it's Thanksgiving," said a broker at a French institution in London. Implied volatility of March options started the week around 8.9 percent.
He said volatility could head down to around 8.0 percent, a natural support line, before pushing back up again.
Among trades, was 124.50/128.50 combo, the broker said. An Italian bank bought the 128.50 calls and sold the 124.50 puts.
"They're basically putting on a bullish trade," he said.
December Italian bond futures on LIFFE were quoted at 127.57, down 29 basis points from Wednesday's settlement.
